key_insight: RSOM reformulates analytic continuation as dictionary learning, uncovering a sparse representation that turns a severely ill-conditioned inverse problem into a much better-conditioned low-dimensional one.
engineering_relevance: This provides a new computational strategy for extracting real-frequency physics from QMC data, with potential impact on simulation workflows that depend on stable spectral reconstruction.
method: Recasts analytic continuation as a regularized stochastic optimization problem.
Learns a sparse dictionary to represent the solution in a compact latent space.
Combines ideas from stochastic methods, regularization, and parameterized models into one framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive performance on standard synthetic benchmarks and on real QMC data from the finite-temperature electron gas.
watch_item: Dictionary learning may improve conditioning, but practical performance will still depend on data quality, dictionary identifiability, and careful tuning of regularization/optimization settings.
paper_title: Discovering a well-conditioned analytic continuation problem via dictionary learning
